These suppressions are NOT code-quality issues to flag during review — they are an agreed-upon, documented mechanism (stated in the PR's "Special notes for reviewer" section) for incremental cleanup. Do not suggest removing or consolidating these suppressions in the same PR; they are addressed in dedicated follow-up PRs.

In RedHatQE/openshift-virtualization-tests, when a PR enables a new Ruff/lint rule (e.g., PLC0415 import-outside-top-level) and annotates pre-existing violations with `# noqa: <RULE>` as a temporary measure to keep CI green (with follow-up PRs planned for cleanup), do NOT flag those suppressions as issues. The suppressions are intentional, documented in the PR description under "Special notes for reviewer", and should be treated as deferred technical debt — not immediate violations. Only flag `# noqa: PLC0415` suppressions that are newly introduced *without* such documented intent.

In RedHatQE/openshift-virtualization-tests, when a PR enables a new Ruff/lint rule (e.g., PLC0415 — import-outside-top-level), it is explicitly acceptable to annotate pre-existing violations with per-line `# noqa: PLC0415` as a temporary suppression to keep CI green. These suppressions are intentional and documented in the PR description as candidates for follow-up cleanup PRs. Do NOT flag such `# noqa: PLC0415` comments as policy violations in the context of rule-enablement PRs. Blanket `# noqa` and `per-file-ignores` remain disallowed; only targeted single-rule suppressions are permitted as a transitional measure.

In the RedHatQE/openshift-virtualization-tests repository, `@retry` from `timeout_sampler` requires the decorated function to return a truthy value to signal success — the decorator loops via `if sample: return sample`. A function decorated with `@retry` that returns `None` (no return statement) will keep retrying until `TimeoutExpiredError`. Always keep `return True` (or another truthy value) in `@retry`-decorated functions in this codebase; do NOT suggest removing `return True` from such functions on the grounds that callers discard the value.

In the RedHatQE/openshift-virtualization-tests repository (Python 3.14 target), PEP 649 (deferred annotation evaluation using descriptors) is enabled by default. This means type annotations in function signatures are NOT evaluated at function definition time, so types imported only under `TYPE_CHECKING` (e.g., `DynamicClient`) are safe to use directly in signatures like `client: DynamicClient | None = None` without `from __future__ import annotations`. Do NOT flag such patterns as causing `NameError` at runtime; they are valid on Python 3.14.

In the openshift-virtualization-tests repository, when responding to test execution plan requests from openshift-virtualization-qe-bot-3, do NOT use "REQUEST_CHANGES" review type if the PR author has already marked the PR as verified (e.g., with `/verified` command). Test execution plans are informational guides, not blocking requirements. Use COMMENT event for informational test plans, or only REQUEST_CHANGES if there are actual code issues that need to be addressed before merging.

In the openshift-virtualization-tests project utilities/oadp.py, DynamicClient instances are passed as parameters rather than created internally, so kubernetes.config import is not needed for client creation fallback patterns.

In the openshift-virtualization-tests repository, it is acceptable for utilities/ modules to import from tests/network/libs/ (e.g., utilities/network.py importing from tests/network/libs/sriovnetworknode). The libs modules under tests/network/libs/ are library/tool modules, not test code, and this import direction does not violate architectural principles in this codebase.
